title: Walnuts: nutrition and omega-3 content

seo.title: Walnut nutrition: protein, fiber, fat, calories and omega-3
seo.meta_description: 1 ounce of walnuts provides about 185 calories, 4.3 g protein, 1.9 g fiber, 18.5 g fat and roughly 2.5 g of ALA omega-3.
seo.search_intent: Look up walnut nutrition and understand what type of omega-3 walnuts provide.

excerpt: A 1-ounce serving of walnuts provides about 185 calories, 4.3 g of protein, 1.9 g of fiber and 18.5 g of fat. Their distinctive feature among common nuts is ALA: roughly 2.5 g of this plant omega-3 per ounce. ALA is not the EPA or DHA found in fish, but it is an essential fatty acid the body cannot make.
content_html:
Walnuts do not lead common nut rankings for protein or fiber. Their most distinctive nutritional feature sits somewhere else: their fat is especially rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids and provides a meaningful amount of ALA omega-3.

What one serving of walnuts provides

NutrientPer 100 gPer 1 oz
Calories~654~185
Protein~15.2 g~4.3 g
Fat~65.2 g~18.5 g
Fiber~6.7 g~1.9 g
ALA omega-3~9 g~2.5 g

The roughly 185 calories in the ounce come mainly from fat. What sets walnuts apart is not lower energy, but the fatty-acid composition of that fat.

Walnut omega-3 is ALA

Alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) is an essential omega-3. The body can convert some ALA to EPA and then DHA, but conversion is limited.

That means 2.5 g of ALA from walnuts should not be presented as equivalent to 2.5 g of EPA+DHA from fish. They belong to the same omega-3 family but are different molecules with different metabolic pathways.

How meaningful is 2.5 g of ALA?

U.S. Adequate Intake values for ALA are 1.6 g/day for adult men and 1.1 g/day for adult women. One ounce of walnuts therefore provides a concentrated amount of this plant omega-3.

That does not create an EPA+DHA requirement equivalence; it simply shows why walnuts stand out as an ALA source.

Other nuts provide more protein

One ounce of walnuts provides about 4.3 g of protein. Almonds provide around 6 g and pistachios about 5.7 g in the same weight.

The difference is roughly 1.5–1.7 g per serving. Real, but not enough to call walnuts protein-poor; protein simply is not their strongest comparative feature.

They also contain less fiber than almonds or pistachios

An ounce provides about 1.9 g of fiber, compared with roughly 3.5 g in almonds and 2.9 g in pistachios.

If maximizing fiber is the only goal, other nuts rank higher. If the goal is ALA within the nut category, walnuts move to the front.

Total fat is high and mostly unsaturated

More than 60 g of every 100 g of walnuts is fat. Much of it is polyunsaturated, including linoleic omega-6 and ALA omega-3; saturated fat is only around 6 g per 100 g.

That composition explains both their fatty-acid profile and their high calorie density.

Storage matters

The abundance of polyunsaturated fat also makes walnuts more susceptible to oxidation than nuts dominated by monounsaturated fat. Heat, light and oxygen speed rancidity.

An airtight container in a cool, dark place—or refrigeration for longer storage—helps preserve flavor and fat quality.

The practical idea

One ounce of walnuts provides about 2.5 g of ALA omega-3 along with roughly 4.3 g of protein and 1.9 g of fiber. Their nutritional strength is not winning every nut ranking; it is a polyunsaturated-fat profile that few common nuts match.

faq.question: How much omega-3 is in walnuts?
faq.answer: One ounce provides roughly 2.5 g of ALA, the main plant omega-3 in walnuts.

faq.question: Is walnut omega-3 the same as salmon omega-3?
faq.answer: No. Walnuts provide ALA; salmon provides mainly EPA and DHA. The body converts only a limited portion of ALA.
